text:
leah: quick follow-up from the authn/authz sync — posting a concrete proposal for project-scoped service role bindings and a short migration path. PTAL :eyes:

leah: problem we keep running into: opaque long-lived api keys granted at org level -> blast radius too big, poor auditability for service-to-service calls, and an awkward UX for platform teams trying to enforce least-privilege.

michael: could you sketch the core idea?

leah: sure. TL;DR: introduce a first-class service-principal concept that can be bound to project-scoped roles. Two token types: 1) long-lived API key (bootstrap, pinned to a service principal + project), 2) short-lived bearer tokens minted from that key via token-introspect/issue endpoint. Default runtime authn uses short-lived tokens.

devon: how do we map that to existing RBAC? do we need new role primitives?

leah: minimal changes: keep current roles (viewer/editor/admin) but allow bindings to principal:type=service and scope=project:<id>. We'll add an additional binding attribute "origin" so we can differentiate user, pipeline, service, or external-broker.

sanjay: concerns: latency and token churn if we require short-lived tokens everywhere. Also where are we storing session metadata for audits?

leah: valid. plan says: short-lived tokens default to 1h TTL, cached at edge with cache-control keyed by token-id and audience. We already have request-level tracing; we'll record minting events and token:key mapping in the audit log. Key rotation is done at service principal level; rotation invalidates short tokens only when explicitly revoked (or we can emit a shadow revocation list).

emma: example flow?

leah: quick example: 
```
# bootstrap: create service principal and api key (long-lived)
POST /api/service-principals 
body: {"name":"ingest-worker", "project":"proj-42"}
==> returns service_principal_id: sp_abc
POST /api/service-principals/sp_abc/apikeys 
body: {"expires_in":null} 
==> returns apikey: sk_live_... (store in vault)

# runtime: exchange apikey for short token
POST /oauth/token (client_credentials) 
Authorization: Basic sk_live_... 
body: {"scope":"ingest:write", "aud":"ingest-service"} 
==> returns access_token (1h), token_id
```

devon: so clients keep the long-lived key in vault and only use it to obtain tokens occasionally. That reduces blast radius, good. How do we handle cross-project calls?

leah: cross-project calls need explicit grants. Two options: a) grant a service principal a role in multiple projects (explicit), or b) create a short-lived cross-project delegation token issued by an auth-broker that records the parent principal and allowed target scope. We prefer explicit multi-project bindings by default. Brokered delegation is opt-in for platform teams.

michael: migration path for existing API keys? We can't rotate everyone immediately.

leah: migration sketch: phase 0 - accept existing keys as "legacy" service principals with org scope and long TTL; emit warnings in console and require an owner. phase 1 - encourage creation of project-scoped service principals and issue helper CLI to create apikey+token flow. phase 2 - enforce a policy that new keys must be project-scoped. phase 3 - after N months, require rotation or mark legacy keys read-only.

sanjay: audit + compliance: we need immutable mapping in logs from token_id -> service_principal -> project at mint time. Also want KMS/HSM-backed storage for long-lived keys and RBAC checks in the mint endpoint.

leah: agreed. we'll require apikey creation to trigger KMS wrapping and record the key fingerprint in the principal record. Mint endpoint must check the binding and optionally consult a "denylist" or active revocations cache.

emma: what about service identity propagation? if svc A calls svc B, do we include the original principal or the broker's identity?

devon: we should pass the original principal (sub claim) and an "actor" chain: sub -> impersonated_by (if brokered). Baggage trace only. Keep it small.

michael: what are the perf implications for token introspection on every request?

leah: runtime pattern: token verification is local JWT verification for self-contained tokens (signed by our KMS). For opaque tokens we rely on cache+introspect endpoint; we prefer signed tokens for low-latency paths. Minting endpoint returns signed JWTs with short TTL and audience claim so services can verify locally.

sanjay: signed JWTs expose more surface if keys rotate. Need kid and key discovery endpoint, and robust caching.

leah: yep - jwks endpoint, kid header, and server-side key rotation with old keys kept for N hours to avoid immediate breakage. We'll also support compact JWS to keep token size small.

michael: policy language changes? any thought of more expressive constraints (time-of-day, IP, quota)?

leah: out of scope for MVP. We'll add conditionals later (policy engine). For now conditionals can be encoded by role-per-route and platform-level network rules.

ops-bot: reminder: security review required before GA.

emma: one more ops concern: how to revoke a compromised apikey quickly?

leah: revoke flow: mark apikey revoked in DB, add fingerprint to revocation list, invalidate associated short tokens via revocation broadcast (best-effort) and set a global flag so mint endpoint rejects exchanges. Edge caches expire tokens by TTL. For immediate enforcement, services must check token status if the token is >5m old (configurable).

devon: sounds workable. can we draft a short RFC with sequence diagrams and a minimal schema for service_principals, apikeys, token_issues, and audit_event?

leah: yes will draft. plan to share in eng-security next week. action items:
- leah: write RFC + diagrams (due EOW)
- devon: prototype jwt minting + jwks caching in auth service (spike, 2w)
- sanjay: audit schema + KMS integration notes (PR next week)
- michael: migration CLI sketch, help with console warnings

michael: thanks — looks pragmatic. :thumbsup:

leah: thanks all. will post RFC link when ready.
